summary: Firefox’s audio playback clock is being corrected around seeks, reused streams, and repeated playback-rate changes, preventing freezes, A/V drift, and falsely reported underruns. The audio converter can now be configured for resampling quality and handle its buffer type more directly, while shutdown reliably hands pending graph messages to the main thread. _These are largely behind-the-scenes fixes, but they make playback timing and recovery more dependable._
